sectors.name: Technology
themes: Indonesia's digital economy penetration remains below 30%, driving sustained local demand for tech infrastructure and hardware components independent of US rate cycles.
Government push for domestic semiconductor assembly and data-center localization creates structural tailwinds for ID-listed tech names like ELIT and AREA, reducing import dependency.
Global AI capex shifts favor diversified US suppliers (MRVL, LITE) but ID tech outperformance is tied to consumer electronics and e-commerce adoption, not AI hype.
sectors.ai: Buy Indonesian tech selectively: ELIT's +18.9% surge signals local momentum in hardware/component names, while US semis (MRVL, LITE) lag. Favor ID-listed leaders with domestic revenue, avoid chasing US AI names into weakness. Rotate into AREA/NINE for follow-through, trim MSTR on volatility.

Digital asset and fintech platforms (COIN, PADI) are structurally benefiting from rising crypto adoption and payment infrastructure expansion across Southeast Asia.
US financial underperformance (-0.57%) versus Indonesia's resilience highlights a persistent divergence favoring emerging-market financials with higher net interest margins and lower duration risk.
sectors.ai: Buy pullbacks in Indonesia financials, especially BSWD and FUJI, as local outperformance (+0.20%) against US weakness signals domestic liquidity tailwinds. Rotate into high-beta names like COIN and PADI for momentum, but trim CBOE and 2881 into strength. Maintain neutral aggregate exposure, favoring small-cap banks over large caps until US rate volatility subsides.

sectors.name: Mining & Energy
themes: Indonesia's coal export quota system is structurally tightening supply, keeping thermal coal prices elevated and benefiting large exporters with secured allocations.
Nickel downstreaming policy (smelter permits, ore export bans) is creating durable pricing power for integrated producers like ALKA and FPNI amid global EV battery demand growth.
US energy and chemical names (CF, MOS, DOW) are riding a structural re-rating from higher fertilizer and industrial input prices, supported by US infrastructure spending and tight global inventories.
sectors.ai: Buy pullbacks in coal exporters (COAL, DOID) and nickel-linked names (ALKA, FPNI) on Indonesia's export quota tightening and global energy demand resilience; trim chemical laggards (CHEM) into strength. Position for Q3 earnings beats driven by higher thermal coal prices and nickel supply discipline, with stop-losses below 5-day moving averages.

sectors.name: Renewables & Climate-Tech
themes: Indonesia's renewable push under the new administration is accelerating permitting and PPA approvals, structurally favoring domestic players like TOBA and TPIA over US peers.

Global decarbonization capex is bifurcating: US utilities face higher financing costs and regulatory friction, while Indonesian climate-tech names benefit from cheaper capital and state-backed offtake
Green ammonia and geothermal are emerging as Indonesia's durable export-grade advantages, creating multi-year earnings visibility for integrated developers.
sectors.ai: Buy TOBA on geothermal momentum and TPIA on green ammonia optionality; both are insulated from US rate drag. Trim US clean-tech exposure (PCG/EIX) into strength—ID policy tailwinds and domestic demand now dominate alpha. Rotate into LAPD/ARKO for near-term catch-up.

sectors.name: Consumer & FMCG
themes: Rural consumption and tier-2/3 distribution networks are durable growth drivers, insulating FMCG players from urban slowdown and supporting volume-led earnings beats.
Halal-certification and local-brand authenticity premiums are widening, giving Indonesian consumer companies pricing power and margin defense against global competitors.
Digital-native FMCG sub-brands (snacks, beverages, personal care) are scaling faster via social commerce, creating outsized upside for small-caps like COIN and AGAR relative to legacy staples.
sectors.ai: Buy selective FMCG names with rural-distribution and halal-certification moats, as ID outperformance (+0.34%) vs US (-1.06%) confirms domestic demand resilience despite flat aggregates. Rotate into COIN, AGAR, and BRRC on momentum, but take profits on STRK/JARR if volume fades. Favor mid-caps with pricing power over staples exposed to imported input costs.

sectors.name: Healthcare
themes: Indonesia's hospital and clinic operators (MIKA, RSGK) benefit from structural under-penetration of private healthcare and rising middle-class out-of-pocket spending, insulated from US tariff shocks.
Global diagnostics and life-science tools leaders (RVTY, TMO, DHR) gain durable share from biopharma R&D outsourcing and precision-medicine adoption, despite near-term US policy noise.
US CROs (IQV) face margin pressure from drug-pricing reforms and tariff-related supply-chain reconfiguration, warranting a cautious stance until clarity on 2026 guidance emerges.

Watch for MIKA/RSGK earnings confirmation of resilient outpatient volumes before adding.

Consolidation among small-cap media firms (MDIA, IBOS, ARCI) is creating scarcity value and rerating potential as foreign ownership limits tighten and domestic liquidity deepens.

sectors.name: Property & Real Estate
themes: Infrastructure corridors (Jakarta MRT, toll roads) are structurally re-rating adjacent land values, favoring developers with strategic land banks along new transit nodes.
Data-center and logistics land demand is a durable, multi-year driver for industrial-zone owners (GRIA, ARE) as hyperscalers expand in Java and Batam.
Residential affordability remains pressured by high mortgage rates and weak purchasing power, capping upside for mass-market developers (BAPI, ELTY) despite occasional speculative spikes.
sectors.ai: Buy selective Jakarta-land and industrial-zone developers (SWID, GRIA, ARE) on the back of sustained infrastructure spend and data-center land demand; avoid residential laggards (BAPI, ELTY) where inventory overhang persists. Rotate into names with confirmed land-bank monetization catalysts, as the sector's relative outperformance vs. US signals domestic liquidity support, but keep stops tight given rate-cut uncertainty.

sectors.name: Crypto & Digital Assets
themes: Indonesian crypto adoption is structurally driven by high mobile-first retail penetration and remittance demand, making local exchange volume a durable leading indicator for altcoin cycles.
Regulatory clarity under Bappebti and the pending OJK transition will institutionalize custody and payment rails, widening access to digital assets beyond speculative trading.
Global stablecoin settlement infrastructure is increasingly bypassing traditional banking corridors, positioning Indonesia as a high-growth node for cross-border digital payments.
sectors.ai: Rotate into liquid large-cap alts (XRP, ADA, BCH) for sustained upside as global crypto breadth confirms risk-on; treat ENA/PUMP/BTW spikes as momentum traps—trim into strength. Indonesian retail flow will lag but follow BTC dominance breaks; add exposure via regulated local venues before ETF-linked spillover fades.
